summary: Milestone 2026.04.99 closeout was short but still orchestration-bound rather than compute-bound. The supplied timing slice measured 10 minutes of wall time for 2 completed items, averaging 5 minutes per experiment. The only nonzero slow path was the arXiv Bundle v10 lane gated on Exp 1269 critical fixes. Both RTX 3090s were idle at closeout with 4 MB allocated each, 0% utilization, and no compute processes, so the wasted capacity was idle GPU availability rather than zombie VRAM. Pre-flight was not a material bottleneck; serial gate/doc coupling and passive GPU scheduling were the recoverable losses.
wall_time_basis: User-supplied timing block: total milestone wall time 10 minutes / 0.2 hours.

slowest_experiments.title: arXiv Bundle v10 - Gated on Exp 1269 Critical Fixes
slowest_experiments.why_long: This was the serialized paper/arXiv critical path. It could not start until Exp 1269 critical fixes were available, then absorbed the full measured closeout wall time for bundle compilation and upload-pending reconciliation.

slowest_experiments.title: In-process docs for arXiv Bundle v10 - Gated on Exp 1269 Critical Fixes
slowest_experiments.why_long: The supplied timing rounded this to 0 minutes. It was not a measured wall-clock bottleneck, but repeated roadmap/changelog duplication in the repo shows reconciliation should be made idempotent.

bottlenecks_identified: Exp 1270 was the only material slow path, consuming the full 10 minute closeout slice because it was gated on Exp 1269 critical fixes.
GPU utilization was inefficient: both RTX 3090s were idle at closeout despite available DualGPU capacity.
No gpu_monitor.py-class zombie processes were detected. The 4 MB allocations on each GPU were negligible context residue, not material VRAM waste.
The closeout was effectively sequential. CPU/docs work and any GPU-eligible follow-up lanes could have been overlapped once the paper gate state was known.
Pre-flight checks were not a measured bottleneck for this slice; existing changelog evidence records focused checks in seconds rather than minutes.
Documentation reconciliation was cheap in measured time but inefficient operationally because repeated .99 rows and changelog bullets already exist; this points to missing idempotent upsert tooling.
Per-experiment timing and GPU telemetry remain too implicit. The retro depends on supplied timing and post-hoc gpu_monitor.py output instead of structured conductor fields.
improvements_suggested: Use DualGPURunner by default when both RTX 3090s are idle, with one GPU lane for Qwen-class work and one for Gemma-class work.
Split paper/arXiv closeout into explicit gate-check, compile, upload, and docs phases with structured duration fields for each phase.
Emit one structured blocked artifact immediately for gated work instead of letting gated dependencies hold the queue.
Run docs reconciliation asynchronously after terminal artifacts exist, and make changelog/roadmap updates idempotent by milestone and experiment range.
Cache TeX build state and pre-flight test state so repeated closeout passes do not redo unchanged setup work.
Promote scripts/gpu_monitor.py output into conductor scheduling input: if both GPUs are idle and GPU work is queued, launch it or write a clear block reason.
Add per-experiment telemetry fields for first GPU allocation time, peak VRAM, average utilization, pre-flight duration, docs duration, and gate-wait duration.
estimated_time_savings_rationale: A 30% saving is plausible for the next similar closeout: roughly 10% from idempotent docs reconciliation, 5-10% from cached TeX/pre-flight state, and 10-15% from structured gate handling plus active parallel CPU/GPU lanes. On a 10 minute slice this is only about 3 minutes, but the same fixes matter more on longer milestones.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Make changelog and roadmap reconciliation idempotent so repeated retro passes update one record instead of appending duplicates.
Use gpu_monitor.py as active scheduler input and launch DualGPU work whenever both cards are idle and eligible work is queued.
Record structured gate, pre-flight, compile, docs, and GPU timing fields in every experiment artifact.

gpu_utilization.assessment: Inefficient. Both GPUs were idle at closeout; no GPU-bound work was running concurrently with the paper/docs closeout.

zombie_process_assessment.basis: scripts/gpu_monitor.py --json reported an empty processes list and no warnings at 2026-05-04T21:09:55.820260Z. The monitor classifies zombies as processes holding at least 1024 MB for more than 10 minutes with under 1% CPU; no process met that condition.
zombie_process_assessment.material_resource_waste: No material zombie waste. The issue was idle GPUs, not leaked VRAM.

preflight_assessment: Not a bottleneck in the supplied 10 minute closeout slice. Prior .99 changelog evidence records focused 81-test pre-flight checks under roughly 8 seconds, far below the 10 minute arXiv gate/compile path.
doc_reconciliation_assessment: Measured as 0 minutes in the supplied slowest list, so it was not wall-clock dominant. It was still operationally inefficient because multiple .99 roadmap rows and changelog bullets already existed; next milestone should use idempotent reconciliation.
parallelization_assessment: The arXiv bundle itself was gated on Exp 1269 and therefore not parallelizable before that gate passed. Once the gate state was known, docs reconciliation, GPU-eligible experiments, and independent CPU/data tasks could have run in parallel instead of leaving both GPUs idle.

question_answers.which_experiments_took_longest_and_why: Exp 1270 took 10 minutes, the full measured nonzero closeout time, because the arXiv bundle was serialized behind Exp 1269 critical fixes and included bundle/upload-pending reconciliation. Inline docs registered 0 minutes.
question_answers.was_gpu_utilization_efficient: No. Both RTX 3090s were idle at 4 MB allocated and 0% utilization. The closeout ran sequentially rather than using DualGPURunner or a parallel GPU lane.
question_answers.were_there_zombie_processes_wasting_reso: No material zombies were present. gpu_monitor.py reported no GPU processes; the 4 MB allocations do not meet the monitor's zombie threshold.
question_answers.could_any_experiments_have_been_parallel: Yes. The gated arXiv compile could not precede Exp 1269, but docs reconciliation and independent GPU/CPU tasks could have overlapped after the gate status was known.
question_answers.was_the_preflight_test_suite_a_bottlenec: No. Available evidence points to seconds-scale focused checks; the measured bottleneck was the 10 minute arXiv critical path.
question_answers.were_doc_reconciliation_passes_efficient: Not fully. They were cheap in wall time, but repeated .99 rows and duplicate changelog entries show missing idempotency.
question_answers.what_tooling_would_speed_up_the_next_mil: Active GPU-aware scheduling, idempotent docs upserts, structured gate/pre-flight/compile/docs timing, cached TeX and test state, and immediate terminal artifacts for blocked work.

meta_reflection: The skeleton-first requirement did its job: the artifact existed immediately. The operational problem is now refinement quality and idempotency. For the next milestone, the conductor should treat skeletons as crash protection only, then force terminal status, structured timings, and single-record docs reconciliation before closeout.
